summary: Macro, not company news, dominates: the Nasdaq 100 had its worst day since 2020 on 11-05 (S&P down about $3T, VIX up 39%, AI/data-center selloff after the Democratic sweep), and the October payrolls print this morning came in at 165K vs 65K expected with unemployment at 4.1%, which is a hawkish surprise against the earlier December-hike backdrop (that link is my inference; the headline itself does not draw it). Company event risk is thin: no 8-K 4.01, 4.02 or 5.02 and no new 1.01/2.01 anywhere in the 7-day filings (the only 1.01 is LNG's unread 11-03 filing), and the only earnings inside five trading days are SBH (11-10 company-scheduled, file says 11-12) and TTEK (11-11 estimate); held CARG reported 11-05 after the close and its reaction is not in this pre-open input. Applied L2: every symbol in the events file was checked against its own filings and estimate, and several stale file dates (CARG, DBX, ONC, RL, TPR, BJRI) are resolved from 8-K 2.02 filings.

October NFP landed this morning at 165K vs 65K, unemployment 4.1%, with index futures mixed. Continues the 10-23 onward QQQ flags: those graded mostly wrong at 5 days, but the direction was right and today is the confirmation, so treat it as the live backdrop rather than a new event.

Fell about 5% to about $76K on 11-05 ($838M liquidations, crypto-linked equities such as Robinhood sold off); Scaramucci notes it has erased gains since the Nov 2024 election. New regulatory risk: Democrats reportedly want to rewrite the CLARITY Act to expand SEC powers and curb the CFTC, which could delay crypto regulation; Warren is expected to chair Senate Banking from 2027. Smaller items: Core Scientific exiting BTC mining, Datavault AI firing its CEO over a BTC-deal restatement, Greece's 10% crypto-gains tax. Dated catalysts: NFP today and the MSCI crypto-treasury index decision on 11-11. Binance exchange-failure clause: no new exchange failure in this input (Circle and Bitwise defended Binance on 11-04, $2.85B frozen per the 11-04 note), so nothing here trips it. Lessons put the held stop near $75.3K; the 11-05 print of about $76K is close to it, and I do not have today's mark.

notable.headline: Nasdaq 100 worst day since 2020; $3T S&P rout; VIX +39%; Ives 'golden buying opportunity' vs Schiff 'more pain ahead'
notable.read: The AI/data-center-policy selloff flagged since 10-23 has arrived in size. The direction of the standing QQQ flag was right even though it graded wrong at 5 days. Analyst camps split (Ives, Lee and Black buyers; Schiff and Oxford Economics cautious); that is sentiment, not an event. Most other QQQ-tagged items (prediction-market odds, Trump, Cruz, Carson) are noise.

notable.headline: October payrolls smash estimates at 165K vs 65K, jobless rate falls to 4.1%
notable.read: The hard datum Cramer said could 'repeal' the midterm rally. A big upside miss on jobs raises rate-hike risk against the December-hike odds noted earlier (my inference), which matters for TLT, IEF, BND, VNQ, GLD and long-duration tech. Futures were mixed at 13:39Z; the reaction is not yet in the input.

notable.headline: Democrats Reportedly Push CLARITY Act Rewrite to Expand SEC Powers; Warren could chair Senate Banking
notable.read: A regulatory-risk step up for the crypto sleeve: expanded SEC oversight and a delayed rulebook. Continues the 11-05 Capitol Hill probe thread (Trump Media's $342M move to Crypto.com, subpoena risk). Reports only, not enacted.

notable.headline: Bitcoin plunges to $76,000 on $838M liquidations; Scaramucci says BTC has erased gains since Trump's 2024 victory
notable.read: A liquidation-driven drop, a sharp reversal of the post-sweep move above $81K on 11-04. The exchange-failure clause is untripped (no exchange failed; the Binance hack is being defended by Circle and Bitwise). Earlier BTC flags graded mostly wrong at 5 days, so this stays a risk-watch item with NFP and the MSCI 11-11 decision as dated catalysts.

notable.headline: CarGurus Q3 adj EPS $0.70 beats $0.66; Q4 sales guide $258.5M-$263.5M vs $263.5M est; $250M buyback
notable.read: Held through earnings. Beat and buyback are supportive; the Q4 sales guide midpoint is slightly below the estimate and the FY sales guide was only narrowed. Net reads as neutral-to-positive on numbers, but the price reaction is not in this pre-open input, so the 'negative surprise' clause cannot be judged from news alone.

notable.headline: PT cuts after the beat (Goldman $115, UBS $107, Barclays $107, Leerink $104); AM Best places Aetna ratings under review, developing
notable.read: Third day of post-print softness around a beat-and-raise: the cuts keep ratings, so they look like valuation trims plus political overhang (Warren, Labor Department PBM rule), and the AM Best action fits the separation. Echoes the TPR and CLX pattern where pre-print PT cuts did not predict a bad print, but here the cuts come after a good print. Not held per these notes.
